title: Clothes
subtitle: put on, take off, do up
summary: Name the clothes and jewellery people wear, and use the verbs that go with them - put on, take off, do up and change into.

lesson.heading: Smart, stylish and casual
lesson.text: We use three common adjectives to describe the way people dress. Someone who is **stylish** wears nice clothes and looks attractive; we can also say **well-dressed**. Someone who is **smartly dressed** looks clean and tidy in clothes that are right for a formal situation. **Casual** clothes are comfortable and right for informal situations.

examples.text: The woman looks very **stylish** in her new coat.
He was very **smartly dressed** this morning. He had his best suit on.
Jeans and a T-shirt are **casual** clothes.

lesson.heading: Words for clothes
rows: top, skirt, tights, boots, suit, tie, jeans, T-shirt, jumper (also sweater), jacket, scarf, cap, trainers
rucksack (a bag you carry on your back)
lesson.note: A **jumper** and a **sweater** are the same thing. **Trainers** are soft shoes for sport and for everyday wear.

lesson.heading: Getting dressed
lesson.text: When you **put on** your clothes, you **get dressed**. The opposite of **put on** is **take off**. We use these verbs for single items of clothing too.

examples.text: As soon as I get up, I have a shower and **get dressed**.
I had a quick shower, **got dressed**, then joined the others for breakfast.
It took me ages to **put on** these boots.
Why don't you **take off** your coat?

lesson.heading: Do up and undo
lesson.text: You **do up** a zip or a button to close it, and you **undo** it to open it. The past form of undo is **undid**.

examples.text: Julia couldn't **do up** the zip on her jacket.
I prefer jackets with a zip; it's easier to **undo** a zip and much quicker to do it up.
I took my tie off and **undid** the top button of my shirt.

lesson.heading: Colours that suit you and changing your clothes
lesson.text: If a colour **suits** you, you look good in it. The opposite of **dark** colours is **bright** colours. When you get home you often **change into** something more comfortable.

examples.text: I think I look good in black because dark colours **suit** me.
You should wear bright colours more often; they **suit** you.
I **changed into** a pair of jeans as soon as I got home.

lesson.text: We say *I like clothes* (not ~~cloth~~ or ~~cloths~~), and *I like your new trousers* (not ~~trouser~~) - trousers, jeans and tights are always plural.

exercises.prompt: Which one of these is jewellery?
exercises.explanation: Earrings, a necklace, a bracelet and a ring are all jewellery.
We look good in a colour: she looks nice in purple.

exercises.prompt: He was very smartly ___ this morning. He had his best suit on.
exercises.explanation: Smartly dressed = clean and tidy, and right for a formal situation.

exercises.prompt: You should wear bright colours more often; they ___ you.
exercises.explanation: If a colour suits you, you look good in it.

exercises.explanation: You do up a zip or a button to close it.

My brother takes his books to school in a ___. He says it's easier to carry them on his back.
exercises.explanation: A rucksack is a bag you carry on your back.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order to describe a morning routine.
exercises.answer: As soon as I get up, I have a shower and get dressed.

exercises.statement: A man who wears a suit and tie to a formal meeting is smartly dressed.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Smartly dressed means clean, tidy and suitable for a formal situation.

exercises.explanation: The past simple of undo is undid.
